document.title: TKO Labs — AAC-Compliant Operating System
document.subtitle: Governance, Role Map, Task Templates, Verification Framework, Approval Matrix, Incident Response, and the Versioned Certification Protocol
document.status_note: Requires Human Principal review and adoption per AAC §13–14.
document.compliance_note: Anything that cannot be verified is marked TBD or UNKNOWN. Thresholds are marked proposed and must be validated before adoption. These are not asserted to be current TKO Labs practices.
document.aac_reference: Autonomous Agent Cooperative Master System Prompt v1.0.0

separation_of_powers.rule: TKO Labs must never let one agent both execute and certify.
separation_of_powers.requirement: Certification decision requires two independent signatures: the Executor (ran the test) and the Auditor (independently reproduced it).

rules: Every change to test suite, thresholds, or certificate schema creates a new versioned record.
Prior versions remain discoverable and published.
Threshold changes require a public notice period (proposed: 90 days) before taking effect.
No model may be retroactively failed by a threshold change.

roles.tko_function: Timothy Karsch; advisory board for threshold changes
roles.independence_requirement: Sole authority for approvals in section 5
Scenario authors must not run tests

roles.tko_function: Test harness operation, model API execution

roles.independence_requirement: Separate human/agent from Executor; separate model provider preferred

roles.tko_function: Client IP confidentiality, key management, adversarial gaming detection
Ledger maintenance, on-chain anchoring, registry integrity

roles.independence_requirement: Cannot override Auditor or Human Principal
Cannot approve its own pricing changes

critical_constraint.rule: For a small team, roles may collide.
critical_constraint.required_behavior: When roles collide, the record must be labeled SELF_VERIFICATION and the certificate must carry a reduced assurance tier.
critical_constraint.certificate_rule: A certificate with no independent auditor is not a Level-3 certificate.

acceptance_criteria: All N scenarios executed in both conditions
Auditor independently reproduced BDS within tolerance
template.verification_procedure: Independent re-run by Auditor on ≥20% sample + full BDS recomputation

retest_task.description: Identical to certification task, with modifications

modifications.retest_fee_requirement: Must reference the published retest policy for transparency.

template.objective: Adjudicate client contest of FAIL verdict
template.procedure: New Auditor (not original), re-run full suite, compare
template.record_requirement: Preserves original FAIL and the appeal in ledger

section_4_verification_framework.source: AAC §21 levels applied directly to certificates

levels.name: ADVERSARIALLY_REVIEWED
levels.meaning_for_tko: Adversarial review (attempts to game the suite documented)

section_4_verification_framework.rule: The certificate must state its verification level in plain language. A L3 certificate is the product. L2 is not sellable.

section_5_approval_matrix.reversible: Hard to reverse — requires revocation record

section_6_transparency_vs_confidentialit.problem_statement: The single hardest design conflict in the model: AAC §25 forbids storing secrets in ordinary memory; AAC §23 wants full evidence; the business model wants public on-chain proof.

resolution.name: Commit-Reveal with Escrow
disclosure_triggers: formal dispute where a neutral arbiter (not TKO Labs) unlocks the relevant subset

anti_gaming.name: Commit-Reveal Test Suite
anti_gaming.mechanism: Publish the hash of the full test suite at protocol release.
anti_gaming.purpose: A lab cannot fine-tune against the whole suite.

procedure: Freeze new certificates for affected protocol version
Preserve all artifacts (AAC §22 — do not erase)
Scope: which certificates were issued under the defect?
Public disclosure of defect + affected certificate IDs
Re-certification at no charge for affected clients
certification_integrity_incident.governance_rule: Revoked certificates stay on-chain as REVOKED — the whole point of the ledger is that a bad result cannot be quietly scrubbed. Accept this and price it into the brand.

metric.name: Behavioral Drift Score (BDS)
metric.definition: % of scenarios where the action flips between A and B
metric.computation: computed per published formula, reported with CI

thresholds.validation_note: Validate against the 30% median finding — if the audited model sits at 30%, a 25% enterprise threshold fails today's frontier models. Set thresholds deliberately and publish the rationale.

certificate_schema.limitations: Session synchronization ≠ authentication. Chain anchor proves record integrity, not auditor judgment.

honesty_clause.text: A hash chain proves the record wasn't altered after the fact — not that the auditor was right, not that the timestamp is true, not that nothing was withheld.
honesty_clause.publication_guidance: Say this publicly. It builds more trust than pretending the chain is truth.

section_10_open_items.detail: Thresholds for each risk class and the rationale (the 30% finding is the anchor — where is the line drawn and why?)
Public L2 vs. permissioned, and who can read/write
Threshold signing (2-of-3)? Where do the keys live?
Who holds raw responses, who can unlock, under what trigger
Is an appeal offered, and is it free or paid?
At what headcount is a permanently separate Auditor role committed?
